analysis_steps.goal: Build noise and SNR maps and extract MORA sources

method.value: Noise map from minimum noise scaled by the inverse primary beam, or from a 2D boxcar standard deviation after sigma clipping; SNR map = primary-beam-corrected flux map / noise map; candidates found as pixels above a SNR threshold

evidence.loc: 2 Mapping Obscuration to Reionization ALMA (MORA) Survey
evidence.quote: Once we have a noise map, we simply divide the primary beam corrected flux map by this noise mosaic in order to obtain a SNR map

evidence.loc: 2 Mapping Obscuration to Reionization ALMA (MORA) Survey
evidence.quote: This SNR map is then used to find source candidates by searching for pixels above a SNR threshold.

method.value: Simulate Gaussian noise maps, convolve with an average synthesized beam, scale to unit standard deviation, count peaks above threshold with the same source-finding algorithm; repeat 100 times

evidence.quote: the maps are convolved with a beam representative of the average synthesized beam in our observations
This process is repeated 100 times in order to measure the expected number of false sources and its corresponding uncertainty.

key_parameters.value: 100 realizations; contamination distributed among the 13 sources according to their SNRs via a normal probability distribution

evidence.quote: the contamination fraction is distributed among the 13 sources according to their SNRs with a proportionality given by a normal probability distribution

analysis_steps.goal: Measure completeness and flux boosting by source injection

method.value: Insert artificial sources one at a time at random positions in the real maps (bright detections removed), recover with the same extraction procedure; completeness = recovered/inserted; flux boosting = average intrinsic/recovered flux ratio

evidence.quote: The artificial sources are inserted, one at a time, at random positions around the whole mosaic
This is done by estimating the average ratio between the sources’ intrinsic flux density and the recovered flux density in the simulations.

key_parameters.value: Flux density bins of 25 uJy, 10,000 repetitions per bin; recovered if within ~1.5'' (one synthesized beam) of the input position

evidence.quote: In each flux density bin of $25\,\rm\mu Jy$, we repeat this process 10,000 times in order to sample the noise variation across the maps.
A source is considered recovered if it is detected within a synthesized beam from the input position ($\sim1.5''$).

analysis_steps.goal: Derive MORA 2 mm cumulative number counts

method.value: Sum per-source contributions eta_i = (1 - f_cont)/(zeta * A_eff) over sources above each flux density; Monte Carlo over flux density, contamination and completeness uncertainties; Poisson errors added in quadrature

evidence.quote: the cumulative number counts, $N(>S)$, are estimated by the sum over all sources with a flux density higher than $S$
This procedure is repeated 100 times, with the mean values representing the final number counts and the 16th and 85th percentiles their associated confidence interval.

The Psi_2 uncertainty is large and asymmetric, and the SFRD fractions at z=5-6 have large uncertainties
The 3 mm counts rest on a heterogeneous archival sample with revised false-detection rate
